The Boat

Sixty feet of floating sanctuary

Rest & Roam is a lovingly appointed 60ft widebeam, moored on the Trent & Mersey at Shardlow — one of England's most storied canal villages, where the old wharves and warehouses still tell the story of a working waterway. She's wide enough to forget you're afloat, and quiet enough to hear the moorhens.

Come for a night or linger for the week. Whether you're here for the walks, the village pubs, the birdsong at dawn, or simply to let the world unspool for a while — the cut has a way of making everything feel possible again.

On Board

Fitted for comfort,
made for lingering

Every detail has been considered — from the wool throws on the beds to the good coffee waiting in the kitchen. Rest & Roam is a proper home on the water, not a camping trip.

Two Bedrooms

A kingsize in the master cabin, twins in the second. Both dressed in white cotton with wool throws for cool canal mornings.

Full Kitchen

Hob, oven, fridge — everything you'd want. Local eggs and good coffee waiting on your arrival.

Private Bathroom

A proper roll-top bath. Hot power shower. Thick towels. The sort of bathroom you didn't expect to find on a boat.

Saloon Lounge

A log-burning stove, deep sofas, and a shelf of good books. The kind of room you settle into and lose track of the time.

Stern Deck

Your own private patch of sky above the water. Watch the herons, the dog walkers, the slow passage of other boats.

Free WiFi

It's there if you need it. Though once you're sitting on the stern watching the light change on the water, you may find you don't.

The Mooring

Somewhere on
the cut

Rest & Roam doesn't stay still. She moves with the seasons, the weather, and the water — mooring at six handpicked spots along the Trent & Mersey between Sawley and Willington. Each one chosen for character, quiet, and a good pub within walking distance.

Your exact mooring is revealed closer to your stay
01

~4 miles east · via River Trent

Sawley Marina

One of the Midlands' largest marinas. Café on site, Steamboat Inn nearby, towpath walks along the Trent.

Marina facilities Café on site River views
02

Home mooring · Shardlow

Shardlow Wharf

England's finest canal village. Seven pubs within walking distance, convenience store, heritage centre, and the famous old wharves.

Village centre 7 pubs Heritage
03

~2 miles west

Aston-on-Trent

Tranquil moorings above Aston Lock. Quiet village, the Malt Shovel pub a short stroll along the towpath.

Rural & peaceful Towpath walks Pub nearby
04

~4 miles west

Weston-on-Trent

The Plough Inn is canalside. Weston Cliffs shade the towpath with ancient trees — described as one of the finest stretches on the whole canal.

Canalside pub Wooded cliffs River views
05

~7 miles west

Stenson Lock

Moor above the lock. The Bubble Inn is directly canalside — Greek food, roaring fire, ★ 4.3 across 1,300+ reviews.

Lock mooring Bubble Inn Greek food
06

~9 miles west

Willington

Three pubs within minutes of the moorings. The Dragon gastropub is canalside — ★ 4.3 across 3,000+ reviews, open from breakfast.

3 pubs The Dragon Village shops

Getting Here

Shardlow, Derbyshire
on the Trent & Mersey

Shardlow is one of England's best-preserved canal villages — a place of old wharves, handsome Georgian boathouses, and pubs that have been welcoming travellers since the waterways were the motorways of their age. We're moored right on the cut, a short walk from the village heart.

Easy to reach by car from Derby, Nottingham, or the M1. Full mooring directions and a what's-on guide are sent with every booking.

Derby city centre — 9 miles
Nottingham — 14 miles
M1 Junction 24 — 4 miles
Towpath walks from the door
Village pubs within walking distance
